note: Short English summaries of real provisions, written for testing an evaluation platform. They are abridged and are not legal advice or authoritative text.

provisions.title: Notice periods for employment relationships
provisions.text: An employment relationship may be terminated with four weeks' notice to the 15th or to the end of a calendar month. For termination by the employer the notice period is one month after two years of employment, two months after five years, three months after eight years, four months after ten years, five months after twelve years, six months after fifteen years and seven months after twenty years, in each case to the end of a calendar month.

provisions.title: Written form of termination
provisions.text: Termination of an employment relationship by notice or by termination agreement requires written form to be effective; electronic form is excluded, so an email or a scanned signature does not suffice.

provisions.title: Termination without notice for cause
provisions.text: Either party may terminate a service relationship without notice for cause if continuing it until the end of the notice period cannot reasonably be expected. Termination must take place within two weeks after the person entitled learns of the decisive facts.

provisions.title: Regular limitation period
provisions.text: The regular limitation period is three years.

provisions.title: Commencement of the regular limitation period
provisions.text: The regular limitation period begins at the end of the year in which the claim arose and the creditor obtained knowledge, or would have obtained knowledge without gross negligence, of the circumstances giving rise to the claim and of the identity of the obligor.

provisions.title: Default interest
provisions.text: A money debt bears interest during default. The default interest rate is five percentage points above the base rate per year. In legal transactions to which a consumer is not a party, the rate for claims for payment is nine percentage points above the base rate, and the creditor may also claim a lump sum of 40 euros.

provisions.title: Review of standard business terms
provisions.text: Provisions in standard business terms are ineffective if, contrary to the requirement of good faith, they unreasonably disadvantage the other party.

provisions.title: Exclusion of liability in standard terms
provisions.text: In standard business terms, an exclusion or limitation of liability for injury to life, body or health caused by negligence, and for other damage caused by gross negligence or intent, is ineffective.

provisions.title: Socially unjustified dismissal
provisions.text: Dismissal of an employee whose employment has lasted more than six months without interruption in the same business is ineffective if it is not socially justified.

provisions.title: Scope of the Dismissal Protection Act
provisions.text: The general dismissal protection rules apply in businesses that regularly employ more than ten employees, not counting trainees.

provisions.title: Notice periods for salaried employees
provisions.text: The employer may terminate with six weeks' notice to the end of a calendar quarter. The notice period rises to two months after two years of service, three months after five years, four months after fifteen years and five months after twenty-five years. It may be agreed that the period ends on the 15th or the last day of a calendar month. The employee may terminate with one month's notice to the last day of a calendar month.

provisions.title: Limitation of damages claims
provisions.text: A claim for damages is time-barred three years after the injured party learned of the damage and of the person who caused it. Without such knowledge the claim lapses after thirty years.

provisions.title: Default interest between businesses
provisions.text: In business transactions between entrepreneurs, default interest on money claims is 9.2 percentage points above the base rate per year.

provisions.title: Statutory interest
provisions.text: Unless otherwise agreed, statutory interest under civil law is four percent per year.

provisions.title: Notice periods for employment contracts
provisions.text: Notice ends on the last day of a month. The employer must observe a notice period of one month if the contract has lasted less than five years, two months after five years, three months after ten years and four months after fifteen years. The employee's notice period is one month.

provisions.title: Reasonable ground for dismissal
provisions.text: The employer may terminate the employment contract only if there is a reasonable ground and reassignment within a reasonable period is not possible or not appropriate.

provisions.title: Limitation of damages claims
provisions.text: A claim for damages is time-barred five years after the day on which the injured party became aware of both the damage and the person liable, and in any event twenty years after the event that caused the damage.

provisions.title: Statutory commercial interest
provisions.text: In commercial agreements the debtor in default owes statutory commercial interest of eight percentage points above the ECB reference rate, the main refinancing rate of the European Central Bank.

provisions.title: Voidable general terms
provisions.text: A provision in general terms and conditions is voidable if it is unreasonably onerous to the other party.

provisions.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
provisions.text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the competent supervisory authority, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

provisions.title: Communication of a breach to the data subject
provisions.text: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate it to the data subject without undue delay.

provisions.title: Time limit for answering data subject requests
provisions.text: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request. That period may be extended by two further months where necessary.

provisions.title: Processor
provisions.text: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract that sets out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the processing and binds the processor to act only on documented instructions from the controller.

provisions.title: Administrative fines
provisions.text: Infringements of the basic principles for processing and of data subjects' rights are subject to administrative fines up to 20 million euros, or in the case of an undertaking up to four percent of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.
